value.body: An auditor checks a company's accounts, records and internal controls to confirm that they are accurate and follow the law and accounting standards. Employers include CA firms, audit and advisory firms, banks, and the internal audit teams of companies. A typical day involves sampling transactions, matching them with documents, testing controls and writing up findings.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com with CA articleship, or CA/CMA qualification

items.label: Statutory audit
items.value: Signed by a practising Chartered Accountant
items.note: Internal audit roles are open to other qualifications too

value.title: How you get in
value.body: The usual route is CA articleship in an audit firm while studying for CA; freshers start as audit assistants or article trainees. B.Com graduates without CA can join internal audit or audit support roles and add CMA, CIA or similar later.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Accounting standards and company law basics

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is seasonal, with heavy peaks around financial-year-end and filing deadlines.
Next roles: senior auditor, audit manager, internal audit or risk roles.
Only a qualified CA can sign a statutory audit report.
